claim.summary: For a multiset of points rho = beta + i gamma in 0 < beta < 1, closed under rho -> 1 - conj(rho), with at most A log(k + 2) points of height k <= |gamma| < k + 1 for each integer k >= 0, w = 1 - 1/rho and Lambda_n = sum of m Re(1 - w^n): (1) the sum converges absolutely and equals the on-line part S_on(n) = sum m (1 - cos n theta) >= 0 plus, over off-line pairs, m (2 - (r^n + r^-n) cos n phi); (2) for n >= 1, Lambda_n >= S_on(n) - 4 sum over off-line pairs with |gamma| <= sqrt(n) of m sinh^2(n tau/2) - 5 A sqrt(n) log(n + 2), tau = delta/(min(beta, 1 - beta)^2 + gamma^2); (3) if no off-line point has |gamma| <= sqrt(n) then Lambda_n >= S_on(n) - 5 A sqrt(n) log(n + 2).
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof: the pair formulas and the bound per pair are those of the Li coefficient threshold, which use no finiteness; a pair above height sqrt(n) has n tau < 1/2 and lowers the sum by at most 1.03 m n^2/(4 gamma^4), and the count sums these to at most 5 A sqrt(n) log(n + 2). The height sqrt(n) and the order of the error are those of Lagarias's unconditional formula for the prime side (arXiv math/0404394, Theorem 6.1, read in its statement, with one sign as printed corrected in the entry). For zeta it rests on a local count and on the identification of Lambda_n with Li's coefficient, neither proved here. No novelty.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Shows, in one direction, that off-line points above height sqrt(n) lower Li's coefficient at index n by at most a polynomial error, so a lower bound at that index is not threatened by them.
significance.next_action: Verify the two-sided form and the strictness argument; read the statement of Bombieri and Lagarias on one-sided bounds.

claim.summary: For a finite multiset of complex points other than 0 and 1, closed under conjugation and rho -> 1 - conj(rho), with lambda_n = sum m(1 - (1 - 1/rho)^n): lambda_n = S_on(n) + sum over off-line pairs of m(2 - (r^n + r^-n) cos n phi) with S_on >= 0; with tau = delta/(min(beta, 1-beta)^2 + gamma^2), lambda_n >= S_on(n) - 4 sum m sinh^2(n tau/2), so for n <= 1/tau_max the off-line pairs lower lambda_n by less than 1.09 each and lambda_n < 0 forces n tau_max > log(S_on(n)/M_off); and any off-line point makes lambda_n negative for infinitely many n.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof (partner pairs have reciprocal-conjugate w; Dirichlet simultaneous approximation for the last part). Finite model of Li's criterion with the index threshold of order gamma^2/delta for a pair at height gamma and distance delta. Nothing is derived about the coefficients of zeta; the criterion's sources are not read.

claim.summary: Setting of the tilted inequality reach (F, Phi, T_S), tilt a in (-1/2, 1/2), p = 1/2 - a; S a multiset, finite or not, of points 1/2 + delta_rho + i gamma_rho with a < delta_rho <= delta < 1/2, c = delta - a, such that for every real t the points with |gamma_rho - t| <= 1 number at most kappa log(|t| + 3) with multiplicity. (1) For Re w in [-c, 0) and Im w = u: |Re F(w)| <= b(u) = min(Phi(c), K/u^2), K = c + (1 + e^(cL))/L. (2) For every real t, sum_S m_rho b(t - gamma_rho) <= kappa [Phi(c) log(|t| + 3) + 2K (1.645 log(|t| + 4) + 1.9)]; so the sum defining T_S converges absolutely. (3) If cL >= 2, |tau| >= 6p and (1/2 - delta) L >= log(kappa (87 + 33 log(|tau| + 4))) + 2 log(p/c), then T_S(tau) >= 0.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof: the real part of F is 1/w plus a term of modulus at most (1 + e^(cL))/(L|w|^2), so it decays like the inverse square of the height and is summable against a logarithmic local count, shell by shell; the pole's term 2.25 Phi(p) of the reach proposition then exceeds the points' by the factor e^((1/2 - delta)L) against kappa log|tau|. It bounds each point's term in absolute value. One instance at a negative tilt with 8003 points, at most three in a window of length two away from its pair, computed directly at four heights: T_S is 3.3e6 and the points' part at most 5.4e3.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Covers what the reach proposition and its local form do not: configurations with infinitely many points to the right of the tilt, as the zeros of zeta at a negative tilt. With the conditional explicit formula it says that the three-four-one inequality with a triangle weight of length L, every nonnegative term dropped, is satisfied by every configuration with a logarithmic local count at a tilt in (-1/2, delta - 2/L] meeting the condition of (3), and at all those tilts once (1/2 - delta)L >= log(kappa(87 + 33 log(|tau| + 4))) + 2 log(1 + (1/2 - delta)L/2). An upper bound for what negative tilts can add; shorter lengths and tilts nearer delta are not covered.

relationships.note: A companion of the tilted inequality reach and the tilted local reach for infinite configurations; neither implies the other. The explicit formula for the Riesz mean from the real-part identity for xi'/xi alone, and the tilted reach in two strata: new relationship with prop:tilted-stratified-reach. In a model of prime sums at one height: a point rightmost in the whole configuration shows on a window of lengths unless the other points near its height carry a weighted count of at least its multiplicity; a progression that hides; the link to weighted prime sums: new relationship with prop:rightmost-point-window-criterion. Li height window: new relationship with prop:li-height-window.

claim.summary: Under premise X of the Riesz mean formula from one premise (xi entire with the nontrivial zeros as its zeros and Re xi'/xi(s) = sum m_rho (sigma - beta)/|s - rho|^2) and the strip hypothesis, classical and imported, that every nontrivial zero has 0 < beta < 1. (1) For every real t the zeros with |gamma - t| <= 1 number at most 9 + (5/4) log(|t| + 2), with multiplicity. (2) If 1/2 <= theta <= 1 and every nontrivial zero has beta <= theta, then for tau >= 2 and tau <= y < y' <= 2y: |sum over y < n <= y' of Lambda(n) n^(-i tau)| <= C (y^theta log^2(tau + 2) + y tau^-1 log(2y)), C an absolute constant. (3) Hence for theta < 1 and y >= tau^(1/(1 - theta)) the sum is at most 8C y tau^-1 log^2 y; at theta = 1/2, the Riemann hypothesis, this is the premise of the sparse off-line exclusion with A = 2 for tau >= 2 and y >= tau^2.
claim.assessment: Conditional on premise X and the strip hypothesis, with a complete deduction: the count from the real part of xi'/xi at 2 + it and the series of the digamma function; the sum over a sharp interval compared with a trapezoid of ramps 1/tau, the edges bounded by Lambda(n) <= log n; the trapezoid as a second difference of the record's Riesz means, whose terms at a zero are bounded three ways and summed with the count. Classical in kind; not new. It shows that the conditional exclusion's premise follows from the goal from length tau^2 on; with a weaker bound on the zeros this argument gives it from a longer length, and that no shorter length is possible is not proved. The constant C is not computed. It gives no approach to the goal.
